name: Question 10
problem:
Which of the following is equivalent to 
${\int }_{-1}^{1}\frac{\text{d}x}{{x}^{3}+1}?$
worked_solution:
This is an improper integral of the second kind because the function under the integral is unbounded as we approach the *lower* integration limit from any point that lies in the interval $x\in (-1,1):$

$$
f(x)=\frac{1}{{x}^{3}+1}\to \infty \,\text{as}\,x\to (-1)^{+}
$$

We can attempt to evaluate this integral by integrating $f(x)$ over the interval $x\in [a,1]$ and taking the limit as $a\to (-1)^{+}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}\frac{1}{{x}^{3}+1}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{a\to (-1)^{+}}({\int }_{a}^{1}\frac{1}{{x}^{3}+1}\,\text{d}x)\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following is equivalent to ∫−11dxx3+1?

a
lima→+∞(∫−1a1x3+1dx)
b
lima→0+(∫a11x3+1dx)
c
lima→(−1)+(∫a11x3+1dx)
d
lima→0−(∫a11x3+1dx)
e
lima→−∞(∫a11x3+1dx)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

This is an improper integral of the second kind because the function under the integral is unbounded as we approach the lower integration limit from any point that lies in the interval x∈(−1,1): f(x)=1x3+1→∞asx→(−1)+ We can attempt to evaluate this integral by integrating f(x) over the interval x∈[a,1] and taking the limit as a→(−1)+: ∫−111x3+1dx=lima→(−1)+(∫a11x3+1dx)
